quest.title: A Gifted Rose: Can Stones Bloom
quest.description: Affan's flowers still haven't sprouted. Try to help the disappointed fellow.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Delicious Shawarma Wrap x2, Delicious Tahchin x2, Glabrous Beans x2

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: ♪Rose, oh rose, grant me my wish...

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Hmm? You're still here?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Well, anyway, I'm an old weirdo, and "old weirdos behave in inexplicable ways." Few people ask me questions like you do.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've always wanted to go out and grab the chance to do something with my life.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: When I was a newlywed, I almost left with the Eremites, but then I thought about it, and I couldn't just leave my wife to take up a life of wandering.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Later, I met a traveling merchant and wanted to follow suit and do some business, but that didn't work out because I didn't have enough Mora.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Much later, my wife passed and nothing held me back anymore, but by then, I'd gotten too old to leave.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've dragged things out up till now and I've missed out on too much.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: In retrospect, I've found that I belong neither to this village, nor to anywhere else.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: So in the end, I moved by myself to the edge of the village, and I found life here to be more comfortable.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: And decades went by, just like that.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I'd like to invite you to come and see these flowers when they bloom. It's probably going to be tomorrow or the day after. Will you be able to make it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Alright, alright...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: ♪Rose, oh rose, grant me my wish...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Only outsiders ask about the old ghost. The children of the village all know his name.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Whenever a child is naughty, their parents will say, "The old ghost will come take you away."

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: These younglings don't know the old ghost at all, but are pretty good at using his name to scare people.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I met the old ghost myself as a child. He did dislike children, but he wasn't scary.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: For some reason, he became known as the old ghost. I thought it was just a bunch of people talking about him behind his back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Weren't you friends?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: When I was young, I used to sneak close to his garden to play. He'd chase me away with a garden hoe as soon as he saw me.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He probably took me for a naughty child looking to cause trouble. Why would he remember me?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He might not have known who I was, but I still remember him and his little garden.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: So I suppose I can call him my friend, right?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I want to grow the same flowers, just to recreate that little garden in my memories.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are the seeds doing?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: None of them have sprouted yet.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I've checked the surface of the seeds, and there's not even the slightest hint of germination.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Why is that?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I'm sure these are the right seeds. I found them in the storeroom based on the old ghost's notes.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: According to his notes, the seeds have a long shelf life, and they won't ever go bad so long as they're kept dry.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: And there shouldn't be any problems with the way I planted them either. I watered and fertilized them as I should... So why?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Why don't we wait a little longer, Grandpa Affan?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Every time the two of us go to pick fruits and flowers in the wild, we have to wait several days for them to grow back after we pick 'em up.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Ah, I suppose I will just have to wait. Do you guys have time today? Can you help me water them again?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: It took me hours to loosen the soil in the nursery and I'm too tired to run back for water.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I'll keep watering them and feeding them fertilizer... But really, will it work out...?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I don't know anymore. *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: After dawdling for so long, I've finally decided to do something, and yet I still can't do it.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I failed to fulfill your wish, old ghost. I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grandpa Affan...

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Thank you for the day, children.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Uncle Shafaqat. I wasn't able to fulfill your last wish...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Ah yes, you children were pestering me about the old ghost, weren't you? Well, that's not his real name. I mean, who would actually be called that?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I heard from my elders that his name was Shafaqat. He left Sumeru City when he was young and came to our village.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He built this house after arriving here and lived in it by himself, and for decades, he barely left.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've never seen him as a young man, but they say that he didn't really dislike children at that time.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: He grew many trees and flowers in the front and back yard of his house. Children liked to run over to his place and ask for Ajilenakh Nuts, and also to listen to him talk.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: But by the time I met him, he'd already become old and was called the old ghost, and he'd also come to dislike children.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There must be another way.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: What other way can there be?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Uncle Shafaqat... That old geezer's already passed away in peace. If he was still alive, I could ask him what special methods could be used to cultivate these roses.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Who can I ask now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I know an Amurta researcher named Sabbah.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Oh, you mean that outsider girl. Can she help?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Besides, she came by here before and I drove her away. Will she still be willing to help?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll give it a shot.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: You're a good kid. It's alright if you can't find anyone to help. The thought is enough for me.

choices.text: Why are you so obsessed with growing flowers?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Once in a while, some outsiders would be forced to settle here in our village.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Some people never got used to living here, even if they kept pushing themselves to do so, and so they ended up alone for the rest of their lives.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: That old geezer Uncle Shafaqat was probably one of them. Everyone just accepted this state of affairs over time.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: But no matter how many years passed, I refused to get used to such a thing. It's really such a pity, what happened to him...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: You would have loved his garden too if you ever saw it. Pretty flowers of all kinds of colors, and so many trees of varying heights...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: The person who cultivated such a great garden passed away so quietly. And the only thing people would remember about him now is that the old ghost would take away naughty children.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I refuse to accept this. He wrote in his notes that he wanted these roses to grow everywhere. And I want to fulfill his wish.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I'm old anyway, so I don't care how others may see me. My life will be worth it if I can do this.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've cleaned up his house for him and sorted out the large pile of booklets he'd left behind.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I can show you a volume or two if you're interested.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I'll put these notes <color=#00E1FFFF>in front of the house</color>, just so he can see the sun for a bit through them.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Here for a chat? I've been wanting to talk to somebody.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Affan...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Hmm? Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Sabbah about the difficulties Affan has encountered.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I see, so that's why you have come to me for help.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I'm honored that I am the one you thought of when something like this came up.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: That said, I did not specialize in plant cultivation, and my experience is limited. I'm not sure that I'll be of much help.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Still, I will try my best. The gentleman you mentioned who cultivated a new species of rose also interests me.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I will visit Mr. Affan's nursery when I have some time. You can look for me there later.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Have I really been planting stones all along?
